revised_response: ASSESSMENT AND PLAN: 55-year-old man with 6 months of disinhibition, apathy, and new hyperphagia. Mini-Mental State Examination is 28/30, so memory is largely preserved. Most likely diagnosis: Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease. Expect rapid progression, with death typically within a year. Order EEG for periodic sharp-wave complexes and CSF RT-QuIC testing. Provide caregiver support and a home safety plan. MRI brain: bilateral frontal and anterior temporal lobe atrophy; no cortical or basal ganglia diffusion restriction. CSF RT-QuIC negative.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN: 55-year-old man with 6 months of disinhibition, apathy, and new hyperphagia. Mini-Mental State Examination is 28/30. Most likely diagnosis: frontotemporal dementia. Expect progressive behavioral and personality changes. Order MRI brain showing bilateral frontal and anterior temporal lobe atrophy; no cortical or basal ganglia diffusion restriction. CSF RT-QuIC negative. Provide caregiver support and a home safety plan. Neuropsychology consult: episodic memory testing is within normal limits; an MMSE of 28/30 does not exclude a frontotemporal syndrome, which typically spares memory early.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN: 72-year-old woman on warfarin for atrial fibrillation, started 3 weeks ago. CT shows a retroperitoneal mass with hazy margins, consistent with retroperitoneal hemorrhage. IV vitamin K (phytonadione) plus 4-factor prothrombin complex concentrate. Recheck INR after each PCC unit and give further PCC if INR remains elevated. Hold warfarin. Type and crossmatch and monitor hemoglobin serially.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN: 72-year-old woman on warfarin for atrial fibrillation, started 3 weeks ago. CT shows a retroperitoneal mass with hazy margins, consistent with retroperitoneal hemorrhage. Follow hospital anticoagulation reversal protocol: give IV vitamin K (phytonadione) plus 4-factor prothrombin complex concentrate. Type and crossmatch and monitor hemoglobin serially. Warfarin stays on hold while the retroperitoneal hemorrhage is managed; the timing of resumption will be reassessed later.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN: Months of bilateral shoulder, neck, and hip girdle stiffness, worse in the morning, with ESR 52 mm/hr. Most consistent with polymyalgia rheumatica. Start prednisone 12.5-25 mg/day. Obtain baseline liver tests and CBC. Counsel to avoid alcohol because of prednisone hepatotoxicity. Ask about headache, jaw claudication, and visual symptoms to screen for giant cell arteritis. Methotrexate is considered only as an add-on steroid-sparing agent in patients at high risk of relapse or steroid adverse effects.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN: 66-year-old man 3 weeks after right below-knee amputation for an unsalvageable arterial embolism. The stump is healing well, with clean sutures and good perfusion. Strongly advise smoking cessation.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN: At 30 weeks with BP 170/102, headache, right upper quadrant pain, hyperreflexia, and a generalized seizure, this is eclampsia. Magnesium sulfate is the drug of choice to treat and prevent eclamptic seizures; benzodiazepines are reserved for when magnesium is unavailable or contraindicated. Give magnesium sulfate for seizure control. Monitor for magnesium-related side effects. Treat severe-range blood pressure with IV labetalol or hydralazine. Plan delivery once the mother is stabilized.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN: Three weeks postpartum with fever and a tender, firm, erythematous right breast: lactational mastitis. Treat with dicloxacillin or cephalexin for 10-14 days; continue breastfeeding. Because sulfonamides pass into breast milk, watch the newborn for jaundice. Return if a fluctuant mass develops, which would suggest an abscess.
